articles.headline: You Can’t Cheat At The Chicken Game Anymore In Zelda: Ocarina Of Time
keyFacts: Players could previously cheat at the Cucco minigame in Zelda: Ocarina of Time by moving the chickens into a corner before starting.
The author reported that this specific cheat no longer works in the remake because Talon shuffles the chickens and they cannot be trapped.
The author also noticed that some other exploits were removed, while certain tricks like hitting butterflies with a Deku stick remain.
body: I’d forgotten already (despite playing the original very recently) that Ocarina of Time has aÂ lot of minigames all over the place. There’s Bombchu Bowling (which everyone remembers for its apparently very hot attendant), a game about guessing which chest has a rupee in it, a fishing game, a shooting gallery, and some other stuff. There’s also a simplistic chicken game that rewards you with a precious bottle filled with Lon Lon Milk.
You used to be able to very easily cheat at this game and win it on the first go. Now, in the remake, you can’t.

It’s easy to cheat at the Cucco minigame at Lon Lon Ranch in the original Ocarina of Time. The goal of the game is to find three special Cuccos in a big flock of identical ones inside Talon’s house. Playing normally can take a couple of tries, as you’re given a time limit, and there’s no way of knowing which Cucco is which. And it costs money to play each time, which early in the game can hurt Link’s little baby wallet. But you can cheat by picking up each Cucco in the houseÂ before the minigame starts, and dumping it into the corner behind Talon next to the stairs. The Cuccos will stay back there, so when Talon releases his three special ones, they just sit in the middle of the floor alone and it’s obvious which ones are which.

In the remake, this cheat is gone. Not only can you not get the Cuccos stuck back in that corner anymore (I tried chucking every single one up the stairs, that didn’t work either, they just slid down), but Talon actively shuffles the Cuccos in the whole room when you prompt him to start the game, putting each one back on the floor again. Fortunately, picking up and putting down Cuccos is much faster with the Switch 2 version’s smooth controls, so it’s easier than ever to just…win at this game the first time, no cheating required.

I’ve noticed some other little changes, too, that get rid of well-known little “exploits” if you will. You can’t climb the chains on the drawbridge of Hyrule Castle to collect rupees anymoreâyou just fall straight through them.

On the other hand, some little tricks are still in place. For instance, you can apparently still hit butterflies with a Deku stick to turn them into fairies. I didn’t even know you could do that in the original:
Yessss!! they kept one of my favorite feature from the OG Ocarina of Time. You can turn butterflies into fairies if you hit them with a deku stick!!! pic.twitter.com/yYszJuB58A
— Riz. ðµð¸ (@Rizkhalifa449) November 5, 2026
And, I hear tell you can still do some of the dungeons out of order:

I haven’t gotten there yet, but I’m assuming you’ll still be able to use the Lens of Truth (or Goggles, as I guess they are now) to cheat at the Chest Minigame. Now if only I could also somehow cheat at the shooting gallery…

articles.headline: Keys to victory for the Oregon Ducks vs. Ohio State Buckeyes
keyFacts: No. 23 Oregon visits No. 12 Ohio State with playoff and Big Ten title hopes on the line for both teams.
Quarterback Dylan Raiola avoiding turnovers will be critical for Oregon to pull off the road upset against Ohio State.
Oregon's defense will need to pressure Ohio State's vulnerable offensive line and limit star receiver Jeremiah Smith.
body: Ohio Stadium will be painted Scarlet red when the No. 23 Oregon Ducks arrive in Columbus to take on the No. 12 Ohio State Buckeyes . Playoff and Big Ten hopes are on the line for the new conference rivals, yet the Ducks are sizable underdogs heading into the matchup.

The Ducks are fresh off a thrilling win over Northwestern at home, which saw the offense thrive with aggressive calls from Jay Johnson in the booth, while the defense overcame a slow start and won physically in the fourth quarter. Ohio State, meanwhile, couldn't piece together enough offense in its first start with a freshman backup quarterback, and the defense was shockingly pushed around in a road loss to USC.

Oregon found a way to win as underdogs in their most recent trip to Columbus, back in 2021 , and although the calendar has flipped to November and the stakes are heightened, the Ducks enter in familiar territory. But with a win, Oregon's slim playoff and Big Ten title hopes could suddenly creep back into the land of possibility . However, it all starts with a win over the stout Buckeyes' defense and roster filled with blue-chip talent.

Ohio State has not lost back-to-back regular season games under Ryan Day, and has not done so since 2004. Tackling the Buckeyes on the road, with their backs against the wall, no less, is a tall task. Dan Lanning and the Ducks have some momentum, and could be getting a key part of their offense back for this game. This was the game Oregon had circled on the calendar in the preseason, and despite all the unexpected turns during the season, it's still a highly valuable game for the program, and one that Oregon has a very real path to win.
Let's take a look at three keys to help Oregon pull off the road upset and knock off Ohio State in Columbus.
Let Raiola Build

It would be nice to see the Ducks start fast on offense, but that hasn't been the case often this season, so I wouldn't bet on it against a strong Ohio State defense. Still, I think there is an opportunity for Dylan Raiola to play clean in this game. The Buckeyes don't have a tremendous pass rush, and they haven't snagged many interceptions this season, so there is a chance for Raiola to avoid negative plays.

Lanning said after the win against Northwestern that Raiola feeds off his own confidence, but that can also go the other way. He didn't turn the ball over against the Wildcats, despite nearly losing an early fumble, and since he avoided those mistakes, he was more confident throwing downfield later in the game. Against UCLA, he committed one turnover, then his next throw was way off the mark, and then another turnover, and so forth.

Raiola can't let the snowball gain steam in this game, because Ohio State's defense is going to make a play or two. The Buckeyes are too good not to do so. But, even with the return of Jay Timmons in the nickel this week for Ohio State, there is a blueprint for big plays downfield against this defense, and it can come from play-action and taking what they give you underneath.

If Raiola can avoid having two turnovers in this game, Oregon has a chance to win. But it all depends on how he starts and if he can find early success to thrive in the second half. More than ever, Raiola's play will determine if Oregon has any shot to pull off the upset in Columbus.
Capitalize on Buckeyes' Weak Point

Ohio State's offensive line was under siege last week against USC, and the Buckeyes are dealing with a significant injury up front. Left tackle Ian Moore is listed on the availability report as questionable, although Day did say on Thursday that he believes Moore will be ready to play on Saturday. How much remains to be seen, but regardless, he won't be at full strength against Teitum Tuioti and Matayo Uiagalelei , who have been rolling lately.

Moore's backup, Austin Siereveld, and right tackle Phillip Daniels were the lowest-graded offensive linemen against USC, per PFF, and the Ducks could expose those matchups. Luke Fahey can run a little bit, but he isn't the dynamic running threat that Aidan Chiles posed a week ago. Oregon can cage Fahey in and force him into mistakes if he doesn't get the ball out fast enough.

The Buckeyes did rush for 200 yards last week and can be physical between the tackles, but Bear Alexander and A'Mauri Washington haven't offered many running lanes up the middle this season. If the Ducks can crash on the edges and have safeties and linebacker clean up in the backfield, the Ducks can force Fahey to drop back on later downs or in the second half, and then the Oregon pass rush can really tee off.
Contain Jeremiah Smith, But Don't Forget ...

Jeremiah Smith is the best player on the field in this game. He burned the Ducks twice as a freshman, once in Eugene and again in the Rose Bowl later that season en route to a national championship. The odds are that Smith is going to hurt them again this week, despite Oregon's defense playing well and a freshman quarterback throwing the ball. The 6-foot-4 receiver and Heisman frontrunner is sort of inevitable.

That doesn't mean the Ducks can't limit him. Oregon doesn't often have a corner shadow a receiver, but this might be the game where Brandon Finney Jr. can step out of the nickel and tackle the tall task. He is Oregon's best cover corner in man coverage, and with Koi Perich or another safety bracketing Smith over the top, the Ducks could at least limit the explosive plays.

In his first game with Fahey throwing him the ball, Smith caught 10 passes, but for just 83 yards and a late touchdown. The Buckeyes tried to make things easier on Fahey and give him lots of throws to Smith behind or near the line of scrimmage, hoping to set up blocks in front of him. But that sort of start-and-go offense only allowed the defense time to rally up and drop Smith for a loss or a short gain. Sound familiar? That's very similar to how Drew Mehringer called plays for Dakorien Moore for much of the season.

Ohio State offensive coordinator Arthur Smith could open it up again this week against an Oregon defense that has been beaten by top wideouts this season, but no matter how Oregon chooses to defend Smith, the Ducks do need to keep Devin McCuin and Chris Henry Jr. in mind. They haven't seen nearly as many targets as Smith, but if the Ducks devote too many defenders to Smith, there is probably another receiver open.

articles.headline: Everton v Coventry City: Premier League – live
keyFacts: Everton manager David Moyes is set to equal Harry Catterick's all-time record of 592 matches in charge of the club tonight.
Everton made one change to their starting lineup following their recent win over Newcastle United, bringing in Tyler Dibling.
A victory for Everton tonight could move them above Liverpool or potentially into fourth spot if they win by five goals.
body: … and on that subject, kind of, here’s Andrew Beasley. He crunches the data, and explains why a Coventry win tonight would be a huge deal for Frank Lampard and his Sky Blues.

To the excited chatter of playgrounds up and down the country members of a certain jaded generation, this fixture is a re-run of the 1987 General Motors FA Charity Shield. Coventry, who had won the FA Cup just nine weeks previously, took 35,000 fans to Wembley, a record for the season curtain-raiser, while Everton supporters, making their eighth appearance at the grand old pile in four years, were comparatively thin on the ground. But the latter were the ones who got to celebrate, Wayne Clarke scoring the only goal just before the break, while Kevin Ratcliffe popped Cov’s new £750,000 record signing David Speedie in his pocket. All the post-match talk was of Everton retaining their First Division title: they ended the season in fourth; City, hoping to build on their breakthrough cup win, finished tenth. Both clubs were slightly disappointed with those returns back then; they’d deal on them for this season, right here, right now.

David Moyes = Harry Catterick. Well, not quite: Top Catt did win two league titles (1963 and 1970) and Everton’s first FA Cup in 33 years (1966) after all. But in another way: yes! Our man Tom Garry reports.

With David Moyes tonight set to equal Harry Catterick’s all-time record of 592 matches in charge of Everton across his two spells at the club, his colleague, the Everton women’s team head coach Scott Phelan, has spoken of his fond memories of his role as a ball boy on the day of Moyes’ first match at the helm at Goodison Park in 2002.

Phelan, now aged 38, is a former Everton academy player and he said: “The opportunity to be a ball boy was a big thing. I think I was 14, 15 years of age. Just seeing the players close up, with the best seat in the house, was something I’ll always remember. The sense of occasion, the atmosphere and [Moyes] starting on a positive footing is what I remember.

“What he is about to achieve is really important in his own career but, for this club as well, he’s brought stability in his first and second phase. I have massive respect for him and what he has achieved here.
“He’s had an amazing career. Hopefully he can celebrate with a win.”
Coventry City are in If It Ain’t Broke mode. They’re unchanged following last weekend’s 3-1 home win over Sunderland. Bobby Thomas is getting back up to speed after a calf issue but is not risked.

Everton are coming off the back of two victories over Newcastle United. They can’t play them every week, but they can near as dammit name the same starting XI, which is what’s happened in the wake of Monday night’s 1-0 win on Tyneside: Tyler Dibling comes in for Jake O’Brien, who drops to the bench.

If Everton win this match tonight, they go above Liverpool; if they win it big – five goals big – they leap over Chelsea into fourth spot. Things are going pretty well for David Moyes and his men, who are outperforming expectations that were set miserably low after an underwhelming transfer window. It’s one heck of a turnaround.

But then Coventry City will be pretty pleased with their efforts so far too. After a cold start, they’ve won three of their last five matches, and while nine points and 16th place isn’t exactly the most comfortable state of affairs, there’s been more than enough promise in performances, so spirits remain high as the Sky Blues embark on their first top-flight campaign for a quarter of a century.

Two clubs heading in the right direction, then; two teams and two support bases happy and hopeful. Everton go into this evening’s showdown as favourites, but Coventry have shown plenty of moxie away from home so far, with narrow defeats at Manchester City and Tottenham, plus a win at Nottingham Forest … and they won the last staging of this particular fixture, albeit in the days of Mustapha Hadji and Gary Breen, back on Boxing Day 2000. So they’ll be dreaming of three points too. It could be lots of fun. Kick-off is at 8pm GMT. It’s on!

articles.headline: Windows 11 27H2 is rumored to be a 'full OS swap' with major work therein
keyFacts: Anonymous sources reported that the upcoming Windows 11 27H2 update will be a full operating system swap featuring significant upgrades.
Microsoft will not launch the update as Windows 12, according to reports, though naming plans are not fully finalized.
Microsoft intends to begin testing the Windows 11 27H2 build much earlier than the typical June timeframe used for previous releases.
body: - Windows 11 27H2 is underway and will be a "full OS swap" according to anonymous sources
- Microsoft will stop short of launching it as Windows 12 (but the report doesn't fully rule that idea out)
- Testing will begin a lot earlier with 27H2 next year, compared to the typical June timeframe when Microsoft kicked off previews with 26H2 and 25H2

The next major version of Windows 11 arriving next year will pack some big changes, and what will theoretically be the 27H2 update is set to be very different from the last couple of annual updates for Microsoft's OS, which have been very minor affairs.

The Verge reports that the usual anonymous sources claim that Microsoft is already preparing Windows 11 27H2, and it will be a "full OS swap" with significant upgrades in the same vein as the last major update for the operating system, which debuted in 2024 (and ushered in a new underlying platform for Windows 11).
We're told that there will be a "big focus on quality" with 27H2, and that despite what'll evidently be some sizeable changes, it won't be released as Windows 12.

To mark the big change, we'll be treated to a new default Windows 11 wallpaper (try to contain your excitement), moving away from the 'Bloom' background which has been in place since the OS first launched. Presumably the sequel won't be 'Wilt'. In all seriousness, The Verge shares a design, and the new take is in a similar vein, with blue ribbons amidst wispy clouds. (A hint of the future direction of Windows for consumers, perhaps?).

Microsoft also intends to start testing 27H2 a lot earlier than with the previous two annual releases, which of course only makes sense as with more work involved, it'll require more extensive vetting. Windows Insiders (testers) will get their hands on the first 27H2 build considerably earlier than June, which was when Microsoft kicked off testing with 26H2 and 25H2.
It's also worth noting that in theory, the foundations of 27H2 were laid right back at the start of the year, in moves which already suggested that it's a hefty piece of work.
Analysis: something still bugs me

The Verge report labels next year's big update as Windows 11 27H2, but doesn't completely rule out the idea that Microsoft might still consider a switch to call it Windows 12. It sounds like the naming hasn't been quite finalized at this point.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.

However, it doesn't seem likely, and going for Windows 12 would be too bold a move, I think, as Microsoft really needs to be seen to 'fix Windows 11' as it has promised before looking at the next-gen platform. I don't think the fixing work is nearly done at this point, although Microsoft has made a lot of commendable progress over the course of this year.

Yes, I'm going to bring up the subject of quality assurance (QA) once again, and regular readers of TechRadar will likely recall that I've gone on about this throughout 2026. It's especially relevant if 27H2 is going to be a big update, and you cast your mind back to remember what happened with the last major annual release.

I doubt you'd forget the 24H2 update because it was one of the worst Windows releases I can ever recall for bugginess. There were lots of significant changes – which, as already mentioned, included Germanium, a fresh underlying platform for the OS – and a nightmarish slew of bugs crept in as a result.

This absolutely must not happen with the 27H2 update. Microsoft is trying to reinvent Windows 11, and the reputation of the OS therein, so it's critical to ensure that it doesn't send users trudging into a quagmire of glitches and uncertainty, repeating the miserable march that 24H2 became.

Sadly, I think there's a clear danger that this scenario could come to pass. I still think Microsoft needs to revamp its QA and general testing processes, because even with breaking down Windows 11's feature additions into smaller, more drip-fed chunks, allowing for simple minor annual updates as has been the case in 2025 and 2026, we've still witnessed too much in the way of bugginess.

Stamping all this out should be a key part of the formula to fix Windows 11, alongside performance boosting and memory optimization, as Microsoft moves towards 27H2. It mystifies me that it isn't – and I presume that's the case because there's been no mention of changing QA procedures from Microsoft (only talk of consulting testers more regarding how to change Windows 11 – though of course that's still a great move in itself).

So, Microsoft, if 27H2 is going to be a big update, don't make it a perilous one – get your testing house in order. I do wonder if the hope is that AI advances are going to come to the rescue here, in which case, we could be looking at something doubly perilous, but hey – at least tell us you have a plan to fight back against the bugs, Microsoft. Don't you?

articles.headline: Broncos get noteworthy J.K. Dobbins trade update after RB room news
keyFacts: The Denver Broncos have been linked to running back help at the NFL trade deadline, including potential interest in Jonathan Taylor.
Sports Illustrated reporter Albert Breer stated that a trade involving running back J.K. Dobbins is now unlikely following an injury to RJ Harvey.
Breer reported that Dobbins is expected to remain in Denver and serve as a backup option along with Jonah Coleman until Harvey returns from injured reserve.
body: One of the many teams linked to running back help at the NFL trade deadline is the Denver Broncos. They've been strongly associated with Jonathan Taylor, a player who would cost the Broncos close to a first-round pick in draft compensation to land.

As the Broncos' link to RB help continues with the deadline around the corner, the one player most likely to be impacted by such a trade would be J.K. Dobbins, and not just because his role would diminish.

Dobbins was rumored to be available for trade if the Broncos got someone like Taylor. However, Sports Illustrated's Albert Breer is reporting that, thanks to the injury to RJ Harvey, a Dobbins trade is now not likely to happen, even if they add a RB in a deal.
Broncos not likely to trade J.K. Dobbins after RJ Harvey news
"J.K. Dobbin's name was raised in some trade talks, as Broncos rookie RB Jonah Coleman broke out, but it's less likely now that RJ Harvey is hurt," Breer writes.
Denver was eyeing up running back help even while knowing Coleman, Harvey and Dobbins were all healthy. A blockbuster move for Taylor or a quality move for someone like Tony Pollard was on the table.

Such a trade is still in play for Denver, but now the fallout would look a lot different. With Harvey on IR and out for the next couple of weeks, the Broncos would not likely want to trade Dobbins if they made a trade for a running back.
MORE: NFL insiders reveal four landing spots for Colts’ Jonathan Taylor
Even if the Broncos traded for Taylor, Dobbins and Coleman would factor into the backfield as backup options until Harvey eventually comes back.
While having four quality running backs on the roster might be redundant, it appears likely that Dobbins won't be moved, even if the Broncos find an upgrade to the RB room.

The Broncos are a team to keep an eye on in the trade market, but instead of Dobbins being involved in a potential trade, it seems the veteran RB is going to stick in Denver with Harvey sitting on IR.

articles.headline: Abbott spent years fortifying the Texas border. Hinojosa could undo it all
keyFacts: Gov.-elect Gina Hinojosa could dismantle Gov. Greg Abbott’s $11 billion border security initiatives when she takes office in January 2027.
Hinojosa has previously criticized Operation Lone Star and state cooperation with immigration enforcement, signaling potential rollbacks of walls, buoys, and police deployments.
Border Patrol agents and analysts expressed concern that her election could reduce state support for federal immigration enforcement and border security.
body: Gov. Greg Abbott (R-TX) spent more than five years and $11 billion fortifying the state’s 1,250-mile border with Mexico as millions of people came into the country unlawfully under the Biden administration, but those massive investments may be wiped away when Gov.-elect Gina Hinojosa (D-TX) takes office in January.

Border Patrol agents in Texas and immigration analysts are on edge as they wait to see how the progressive state House legislator will follow through on her campaign statements that disavowed support for how Abbott has sought to secure the border and allow the federal government to carry out immigration enforcement.

Hinojosa has criticized the state’s cooperation with U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement and Abbott’s Operation Lone Star, which was created in 2021 to bolster police presence at the international boundary and inside the state.
In an October statement , Hinojosa said she would “put in the work to secure the border [and] not waste working Texans’ money on political theater.”

However, Abbott’s actions at the border since 2021 go far beyond what Hinojosa has commented on, and everything, at least at the state level, is up for elimination come January 2027 when she is sworn in.
Federal agents and outsiders react to Hinojosa win
A Border Patrol agent in Texas who spoke on the condition of anonymity said Hinojosa’s election was a “punch in the gut” in terms of what it meant for federal agents.

“Abbott was tough on crime especially on the smugglers … and it was always great working with other agencies,” the agent wrote in a text message on Thursday. “But I fear that now Texas will bar any law enforcement working with us like they do in California.”

Ammon Blair, senior fellow for the conservative-leaning Texas Public Policy Foundation and a former decade-long Border Patrol agent, said he “100%” expects Hinojosa to overhaul the state’s plethora of initiatives at the border, setting Texas up for potential problems if cartels try to exploit the borders.

The change in governors was not enough to concern the chairman of the House Homeland Security Subcommittee on Border Security and Enforcement, Rep. Michael Guest (R-MS), who contended that the federal government still controls the border.

“Thanks to House Republicans’ historic reconciliation investments and the Trump Administration’s restoration of the rule of law, DHS has the tools and resources needed to keep our Southwest border secure,” Guest said in a statement to the Washington Examiner . “As some at the state and federal levels try to undo the wins secured for the American people, the Republicans and the Trump Administration will fight to hold the line and will continue to put the safety of our citizens first.”
A portion of border wall is under construction in the Big Bend region, Wednesday, Sept. 23, 2026, near Sierra Blanca, Texas. (AP Photo/John Locher)
A senior Border Patrol official in Texas said the job remains unchanged regardless of who is governor.

“We’re all curious to see what the new administration’s approach to border security will be and whether we’ll continue receiving the same level of state support or see a complete 180,” the official wrote in a text message. “Regardless, the Border Patrol is nonpartisan. We’ve worked under both Republican and Democratic leadership, overcome challenges, and always adapted. Our oath is to the Constitution, and we’ll continue defending our homeland to the best of our ability with whatever resources we have.”
Abbott’s actions
How far Hinojosa chooses to go will depend on the extent that she believes Abbott went too far managing the historic number of immigrants who illegally came across the state’s border with Mexico.

In January 2021, Biden halted hundreds of miles of border wall construction, barred ICE deportation officers from removals, and stopped requiring asylum-seekers to remain in Mexico, among other actions.

Within weeks, the number of people apprehended crossing illegally between the ports of entry rose, particularly in Texas. Rolando Salinas, the Democratic mayor of the border city of Eagle Pass, told the Washington Examiner at the time that he had pleaded with the Biden White House for help as roughly 2,000 illegal immigrants were coming over the border in his town daily. He received no response from Washington.

Migrants who crossed the Rio Grande and entered the United States from Mexico are lined up for processing by U.S. Customs and Border Protection, Saturday, Sept. 23, 2023, in Eagle Pass, Texas. (AP Photo/Eric Gay)

Abbott used state resources to enforce federal immigration laws that he said Biden was failing to uphold as Border Patrol agents intercepted more than 2 million illegal immigrants annually. Unlike Trump’s battles with blue states over immigration enforcement, Abbott attempted to force the federal government to enforce immigration laws.

In March 2021, Abbott launched Operation Lone Star, a statewide initiative that sent more than 10,000 Texas Department of Public Safety state troopers and Texas National Guard members to the border to help Border Patrol catch smugglers moving immigrants across the river and detain illegal immigrants who slipped past federal agents. In addition, the Texas DPS had seized 859 million lethal doses of fentanyl as of Dec. 31, 2025.

“The only state to ever build our own border wall, the only state to not only send thousands of Guard to the border to secure the border, but also we had so many down there,” Abbott said. “We built two military bases on the border to house thousands of National Guard troops, who also have worked to build hundreds of miles of razor border barrier and repel illegal immigrants back into Mexico.”
The state held multiple emergency legislative sessions and passed Senate Bill 4, which the Supreme Court upheld, allowing state police to arrest illegal immigrants on federal charges.

Abbott directed state military and police to transport any illegal immigrants they encountered to the closest port of entry to repatriate them to Mexico rather than turn them over to Border Patrol. As of January, more than 536,000 illegal immigrants have been encountered by state authorities, including more than 61,000 arrested on criminal charges.

A former senior U.S. Customs and Border Protection official who asked to speak on the condition of anonymity said he anticipates SB4 “will likely be targeted for repeal during future state legislative sessions.”

“Border infrastructure deployed by the state of Texas will likely be removed. Both served as a deterrence to illicit cross border activity,” the former official said. “Additionally, Texas law enforcement will likely be restricted from assisting with immigration enforcement activities. All these things helped shape a more secure border environment, which makes the job of a Border Patrol agent safer and more effective.”

Workers continue to deploy large buoys to be used as a border barrier along the banks of the Rio Grande in Eagle Pass, Texas, Wednesday, July 12, 2023. The floating barrier is being deployed in an effort to block migrants from entering Texas from Mexico. (AP Photo/Eric Gay)
The state put up 80 miles of border wall by the end of 2025 and installed just under half a mile worth of buoys in the river along Eagle Pass.
Texas also offered voluntary bus transportation to nearly 120,000 migrants to six cities north of the southern border at a cost of $221 million.
The end of the crisis and post-Biden

Immigrants in Mexico began to bypass the Texas border to instead cross into Arizona and California in the wake of Abbott’s stepped-up enforcement. In 2021, 69% of illegal immigrant arrests across the southern border occurred in Texas, but that share fell to 34% in 2024.

Since Biden left office, Abbott has continued to expand the state’s blueprint for border security. In February 2025, the state allowed roughly 600 National Guard members to be authorized by CBP to carry out select federal immigration enforcement.

Texans are far less likely now to see DPS troopers lined up along the riverbanks, given that the number of people crossing illegally is much more manageable for Border Patrol. But in South and West Texas, troops remain on the roads looking for human smugglers, as well as tracking people on foot traversing the brush.
Inside the state, local and state police may be deputized by federal immigration officers to help them detain and arrest illegal immigrants under what it known as the 287(g) program .
Hinojosa’s ascension

As a state House legislator, Hinojosa voted against the state’s sanctuary cities ban and has opposed deputizing state and local police to assist ICE. She also voted against making illegal border crossing a crime, which means the state-constructed concertina wire and river buoys could be pulled down.

Blair suggested that federal funds given to the Texas governor’s office for distribution to local and state police who assist federal law enforcement at the border under the two-decade-old program, Operation Stonegarden, could also be halted by Hinojosa.
“She can then direct the [State Administrative Agency] not to apply for the next Stonegarden cycle or apply for a reduced amount or attach conditions that discourage local participation,” Blair said.
TEXAS GOP GRAPPLES WITH HISTORIC LOSSES AS DEMOCRATS EYE 2028

Adam Isacson, director of defense oversight for the liberal immigrant advocacy organization the Washington Office for Latin America, suggested that the approaches Democratic governors in Arizona, California, and New Mexico have taken over the years have not led to serious problems that critics had suggested could occur.

“If she does pull back some of the security, it does mean there’ll be less border security, but the number of agents or soldiers or police per mile right now along Texas’s border is so high that it might not even make a difference on the margins,” Isacson said.

articles.headline: Middle East could have big role in Democrats' Trump corruption inquiry
keyFacts: Democratic lawmakers plan to investigate corruption allegations surrounding President Trump and his family's financial links to Middle Eastern countries.
Ethics watchdogs and critics allege that Trump's foreign business deals created conflicts between his private financial interests and public leadership duties.
Representative Robert Garcia said investigating the Trump family, including Jared Kushner's Middle East business activities, is a top priority.
body: Several polls of US voters taken around the recent midterm elections show that an overriding concern about the Trump administration is corruption.
Just days after the midterms, senior figures in the Democratic Party were quick to proclaim that they will be investigating corruption accusations when they take their seats in January.
It's highly likely that many of those investigations will center on the Trump administration's and the Trump family's links to wealthy Middle Eastern countries.

"The incoming Democratic majority in Congress will no doubt aggressively use their powers to investigate the administration's alleged wrongdoings," Amy Hawthorne, a non-resident fellow at the Washington-based think tank, the Arab Center, wrote in a commentary after the midterms. "Cases involving the Middle East will be their top targets."

Financial disclosures made by President Trump in the middle of this year showed that during 2025, his businesses made about $2 billion in income. This was triple the income he reported the previous year, observers noted.

"According to the information available … Middle Eastern countries and businesses have directly contributed to the bottom line of Trump's family businesses — more so than any other region of the world," Brian Katulis, a senior fellow and expert in US foreign policy at the Middle East Institute in Washington, wrote in a July text after the presidential disclosure. "Gulf entities paid around $300 million to the president's businesses in 2025."
Billions in cryptocurrency
A lot of the money Trump made in 2025 came from the sale of a stake in a cryptocurrency company, World Liberty Financial, Katulis noted.

The company was founded by the Trump and Witkoff families in 2024 — Steve Witkoff is Trump's special envoy to the Middle East — and in 2025, a large portion of it was sold to an investment firm backed by a senior United Arab Emirates official, Sheikh Tahnoon bin Zayed Al Nahyan. The latter serves as the UAE's national security advisor and is also the brother of the UAE's president.

The deal was done in January 2026 behind closed doors, shortly before Trump's inauguration as president. In May 2026, the US agreed to allow the UAE access to advanced artificial intelligence chips, despite objections from some national security advisers.
Trump's critics allege a connection, the Trump administration denies it.
There are also other alleged instances of Trump administration corruption with links to the Middle East.
Trump Towers in the Middle East
Various Trump deals with Saudi and Emirati real estate developers are also being questioned because of possible conflicts of interest.

The Gulf real estate developers, which have close ties to their governments and respective royal families, have agreed to build Trump-branded golf resorts, hotels, mansions, skyscrapers and towers in Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Qatar and the Maldives.

In 2025, Trump reported $59.5 million in foreign real estate licensing income, ten times more than he made in 2023, business media outlet CNBC reported in August. Nearly two-thirds of that money came from projects in the Gulf, CNBC said.

Ethics watchdogs argue that, "the deals create conflicts between Trump's political leadership role and private interests" because some of those Gulf states and their developers were also "pursuing major US investments, seeking government permits or pressing for favorable economic and diplomatic relations."
Qatar's flying gift

When the Qatari royal family gifted Trump a luxury jet, worth around $400 million, in May 2025, politicians and ethics experts asked about the propriety of taking such a pricey present from a foreign government.

After his presidency ends, Trump was apparently planning to donate the plane to his Florida-based project, the Donald J. Trump Presidential Library Foundation. Currently, it is unclear whether the Qatari plane will end up there and there's been speculation Trump will try to keep it for personal use.
The library is a non-profit and has received tens of millions in funding — an investigation by the CBS network traced over $100 million in donations — from lawsuits and via corporate donors.

Democratic Senator Elizabeth Warren has already said the library project would be investigated. "Giant corporations and foreign governments should not be able to buy influence in Washington with donations to the president's library," she told CBS.
Gaza's 'Board of Peace'
Plans for the so-called Board of Peace were created in September 2025 and the body was to facilitate a ceasefire and reconstruction in Gaza.

It was set up to be a kind of multilateral international organization, similar to the United Nations, except that Trump would serve as its chairman indefinitely and member countries donating $1 billion if they want to sit on the board permanently.
The Board of Peace has not achieved much in Gaza, experts say, and there have been several worrying developments.

Four months after its establishment, the World Bank account set up to manage Board of Peace funds was empty, the Financial Times newspaper reported in May. Instead, money had been deposited into a private JP Morgan bank account, over which there was no oversight.
There have apparently been contributions of around $3 million from Morocco and $20 million from the UAE, as well as pledges of $7 billion from board members and $10 billion from Trump.

The board's legal status was also changed to make it into an international non-governmental organization. This change in legal status may aim "to avoid US congressional oversight and keep much of its activity opaque," Zaha Hassan, an attorney and senior fellow at the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace, warned in a June commentary. It also "gives Trump ultimate decision-making authority, including over financial matters," she noted.
'Trump crime family'
"The Trump crime family is the top of our investigative priorities," the most senior Democrat on the House Oversight Committee, Robert Garcia, said after the midterms.
And he has already expressed concerns about the behavior of Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner in the Middle East.

Most of the issues around Kushner involve potential conflicts of interest. Kushner is acting as a volunteer envoy in the Middle East and has been deeply involved in negotiations to end the Gaza conflict and the Iran war.
In early October, CNN published an investigation that detailed links between Kushner's private equity company, Affinity Partners, and investments into leading Israeli military manufacturers.
It's also been reported that while he was travelling in the region, Kushner was trying to raise billions for his equity firm.

In March, Democratic politicians, including Garcia, wrote letters to the president's office, saying they had "serious concerns about whether the White House is letting Mr. Kushner use his influence for personal financial gain."
The potentially most damaging claims against Kushner come from a recent book, "Prince and Thieves," published late October by American investigative journalist Matthew Cole.

Cole alleges, "Kushner worked with the UAE to shape US policy across the Middle East and that, in the course of this work, he was given access to bank accounts containing roughly $2 billion," the New York Times wrote in its review.
Kushner denies the allegations about any such slush fund held by an Israeli bank and has threatened to sue Vanity Fair magazine, which published excerpts from the book.
But, as the New York Times concluded, "Cole's work is sufficiently calm, detailed and forensic to necessitate a large-scale and urgent congressional inquiry."

articles.headline: Under Bidzina Ivanishvili, Georgian Dream slowly consumes itself
keyFacts: Georgia’s ruling Georgian Dream party is seeking to outlaw five opposition parties before the 2028 parliamentary elections.
Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze argued that the targeted parties threaten the constitutional order and Georgia's sovereignty.
State Department sources stated that Georgian Dream shows little willingness to change its course despite mounting pressure.
body: Georgia’s ruling Georgian Dream party is seeking to outlaw five opposition parties. It’s a move that would remove competitors ahead of the 2028 parliamentary elections and further reduce freedom in a once exemplary democracy.

The Constitutional Court, filled with Georgian Dream loyalists, began hearing the case in October. The lawsuit targets the parties: United National Movement, Coalition for Change, Strong Georgia-Lelo, the Federalists, and For Georgia. The move would effectively outlaw the country’s main political opposition. It follows successive restrictions on protests, speech, and civil society, alongside the imprisonment and exile of opposition politicians.

“Georgian Dream’s mandate of public trust stands at zero. That is why it has decided to ban its main competitors,” says Tengo Tevzadze, chairman of the Political Council of the Coalition for Change. “This shows change of government through elections in the near future is effectively ruled out, and Georgian Dream has moved to one-party rule … The only instrument left to Georgian society now, together with the banned political parties, is to strengthen the peaceful street protest, intensify it, and build a force strong enough to make Ivanishvili back down.”

The ruling Georgian Dream argues that the targeted parties threaten the constitutional order and Georgia’s sovereignty. Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze has invoked “militant democracy,” arguing that parties hostile to democracy should be denied its protections, and said the aim is to hold the 2028 elections “without agents,” a label Georgian Dream officials routinely apply to opposition figures they accuse of serving Western and American interests.

Bidzina Ivanishvili is a billionaire who made his fortune in Russia, founded Georgian Dream, and is the real decision-maker in the country without holding public office. This move is a demonstration of his power and intent. Since his party came to office in 2012, Ivanishvili has extended his influence over the courts, state institutions, and media. Mounting external pressure, deepening international isolation, and persistent resistance and protests at home are compounding the crisis, and Ivanishvili’s response has been to double down. He wants to convince the public that challenging his rule is futile and reassure his officials that their loyalty remains a safe investment.

The move also has a foreign audience. Ivanishvili wants to convince Washington that his rule is unquestionable and engagement with him unavoidable. The Trump administration has held talks with Georgian Dream, with Tbilisi’s ties to Moscow and Tehran high on the agenda, including a pro-Iranian regime network that is trying to cultivate pro-Iranian sympathies among Georgia’s Shia Azerbaijanis.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio agreed that these are U.S. concerns. Washington has also raised its concerns over the crackdown on liberties. In response, Kobakhidze has complained that Washington engages Armenia and Azerbaijan freely while setting conditions for Georgia. But this complaint ignores how, among many other factors, those neighbors first had to make peace with each other to earn U.S. engagement. Sources at the State Department say that Georgian Dream shows little willingness to change the course. The authorities in Tbilisi want engagement with the U.S. only if it comes free of cost. Ivanishvili, who remains under U.S. and U.K. sanctions, wants relief while keeping his grip on power. The threatened bans give him another bargaining chip. He can later withdraw them and present the retreat as a compromise, while leaving the wider crackdown intact.

Still, the threat of Western sanctions gives Washington leverage over the authorities in Tbilisi. Alarm over personal sanctions may have been a motivating factor for the resignations of two Constitutional Court judges who would otherwise have heard the opposition ban case. And that fear extends beyond the rank and file and reaches into the ruling elite. Many in the party’s leadership have deserted it.

Mamuka Mdinaradze, a prominent party figure and former security chief, quit politics in August, citing a desire to spend more time with his family. Others have met a harsher fate. Former Prime Minister Irakli Garibashvili, once one of Ivanishvili’s closest allies, was jailed for five years in January. Another former Georgian Dream prime minister, Giorgi Gakharia, who split from the party, now faces criminal charges. Authorities portray the prosecutions of former officials as an anti-corruption campaign. But the departures, arrests and public recriminations expose strains within the party elite and suggest that the system Ivanishvili built is becoming increasingly hard to sustain.

“Even if it had held back this lawsuit or tactically chosen to spare some parties and ban others, the course this regime has taken would remain essentially the same,” says Giga Bokeria, chairman of the Federalist party. “It is strengthening Russian and Iranian influence inside the country, cracking down on political liberty, and has declared the entire West an enemy. This course threatens Georgia’s freedom and sovereignty. The way out is to expand peaceful protest until it brings this regime down. That is the task facing our society and the political opposition.”
TRUMP UNVEILS PLAN TO LOOSEN METHANE RULES FOR OIL AND GAS INDUSTRY

Throughout its time in power, the government has used fear as an instrument of control. Georgian Dream warned voters that the West wanted to get them in a war with Russia, and that accommodation with Moscow was the price of peace. Arresting faithful officials carried that fear into the ruling camp itself, signaling that even Ivanishvili’s most loyal lieutenant could fall. Protesters face heavy fines and arrests, and Georgians are policed and prosecuted over what they write online. But taken together, these pressures appear to have eroded Georgian Dream’s support rather than consolidate it.

Ivanishvili may have calculated that a turn away from the West would clear the field, break resistance and leave him free to rule as he pleased. Instead, he has produced a climate in which repression remains his only reliable instrument, and a growing share of Georgians now stand firmly against his rule.

articles.headline: Pope Leo begins 12-Day, 3-country tour after cancer surgery
keyFacts: Pope Leo XIV began a 12-day, three-country trip to South America following recent lung cancer surgery.
Vatican officials said the 71-year-old pontiff completed his recovery period and exhibits "fantastic" stamina for the travel.
The Pope will visit Uruguay first before traveling to Argentina and concluding his journey in Peru.
body: Pope Leo begins 12-Day, 3-country tour after cancer surgery

MONTEVIDEO, Uruguay — In his first trip following lung cancer surgery, Pope Leo XIV has left Rome for what will be his furthest and longest journey: a 12-day, three-country visit to South America. Vatican officials say the 71-year-old pontiff is exhibiting "fantastic" stamina.

Along the way Leo will take 12 flights, including two helicopter rides, give 36 speeches and visit 10 cities including Cusco, Peru, which sits more than 11,000 feet above sea level. Even the heartiest of travellers can experience altitude sickness there and may require supplemental oxygen.
Last month, Leo underwent surgery to remove the lower lobe of his right lung. Vatican officials say he's completed the two-week long recovery period and requires no further treatment.

The Vatican's new communications chief Maria Montserrat Alvar said the pontiff was eager to begin his journey. "His doctors are very confident and he'll have plenty of medical care on board should something happen," she said.
First stop Uruguay

It's a puzzling choice for the first leg of the pope's anticipated return to South America, where he spent two decades in Peru, first as a missionary then as Bishop of the coastal city of Chiclayo. Uruguay, a small nation of around 3.5 million people, where adoring crowds will be small, is famously Latin America's most secular nation.

When asked why go to Uruguay at all, given the high rate of atheists and strict separation of church and state, Communications Chief Alvarado answered simply, "Why Not?" Adding, "the Gospel is meant to go everywhere."

Few welcome banners are seen throughout the capital Montevideo, except for large posters of a waving Pope Leo adorning city churches. A huge banner drapes down the facade of the Blessed Sacrament Church, in Montevideo's upscale Pocitos neighborhood, where 70-year old retiree Ana Maria Saprissa was heading for quiet prayer.
We are thankful, agradecida, she says that the pontiff is coming to visit. "His visit gives us such joy because …he remembered us all here in this tiny country that has so many needs," she said.

Uruguay's tradition of separating religion from government and public life dates back more than a century. Christmas has long been officially referred to as Family Day, while Easter week is given the vacation-friendly name Tourism Week.
Only about a third of Uruguayans identify as Catholics and even less say they practice the religion, according to political analyst Mariana Pomiés , director of the public polling firm CIFRA.

But as a practicing Catholic, Pomies says sometimes Uruguayan and especially officials misinterpret what secularism is. "Secularism is not anti-religion, it's the neutrality of the state in religious matters. But here the neutrality se convirtió en un absoluto… it became an absolute."
Pope celebrates 'positive secularism.'

Dozens of volunteers cleaned streets, mowed lawns and erected a simple stage outside the tiny brick Our Lady of Guadalupe Church. It's the focal spot for many in the Casavalle neighborhood, a working-class city about a half hour north of Montevideo, where the pope is scheduled to visit on Saturday.

"I am very happy, very glad, very grateful … that eyes have been set here," where many are forgotten and stigmatized, said Father Pablo Coimbra who's served as the community's pastoral leader for the past six years

"For the first time many people live their lives always on the margins, on the margins of opportunities, of possibilities, of the future, on the margins of a loving gaze... well, today they are in the heart, in the center," he said.

A proposed papal address to the parliament triggered a swift rebuke from the public and politicos alike and was quickly scrapped. However, Uruguay's left-wing President Yamandú Orsi will oversee a welcome ceremony outside Montevideo's main cathedral, where Leo will later celebrate evening prayers, vespers with church leaders and laypeople.

Sunday mass will take place in Florida, about an hour outside the capital, a town replete with Catholic and national pride. Every Nov. 8, church goers commemorate the Virgin of the Thirty-five, a symbol of Uruguay's independence movement from the Brazilian empire in 1825.
A long awaited Papal return to Argentina
By Sunday, Pope Leo will be in neighboring Argentina, fulfilling a wish of his predecessor, Pope Francis, who had hoped to return to his homeland but never made the trip.
Before his death, Francis had said he didn't want a papal visit to become entangled in Argentina's intensely polarized politics.

Pope Leo's visit to Argentina offers an early test of how he will address the Catholic Church's differences with right-wing populist leaders gaining ground across Latin America. Those tensions have also surfaced in the U.S., where Leo has clashed with President Donald Trump over immigration and the treatment of migrants.
Far-right President Javier Milei's sweeping austerity measures, which have pushed millions of Argentines into poverty, could put him at odds with Leo, who has long championed the poor.

Milei has also embraced data centers and a largely unfettered approach to artificial intelligence regulation, while Pope Leo's inaugural encyclical called for ethical caution and safeguards to protect human dignity in the age of AI.
Saving the best for last?
The final leg of the trip will take Leo back to Peru in what has been billed as a homecoming.

As a missionary priest and later appointed Bishop of the coastal city of Chiclayo, Pope Leo spent two decades in the country. He became a naturalized Peruvian in 2015, and has said the country shaped his life more than anything else.
He will visit several cities and towns where he lived and will meet with President Keiko Fujimori, the daughter of former Peruvian dictator Alberto Fujimori.

As a priest during the Fujimori dictatorship, Leo was openly critical of military violence and human rights abuses and supported efforts leading to Peru's Truth and Reconciliation Commission following the return to democracy.

But for many Uruguayans Pope Leo is not very well known. Walking past the huge stage set up for Leo's welcoming ceremony, Juan Martin Guerreiro said he wasn't sure he would attend the pope's speeches.
"He doesn't feel as influential to me … as Pope Francis," said Guerreiro. But he said he's willing to give the new pope a change because he is South American.
When reminded that Pope Leo was born in Chicago, Guerreiro said he wouldn't hold that against him.

articles.headline: Ilia Topuria accepts Paddy Pimblett’s offer for The Ultimate Fighter showdown
keyFacts: Ilia Topuria said he is interested in coaching against Paddy Pimblett on The Ultimate Fighter before a potential UFC bout.
Topuria stated in an interview that nothing is official yet and he has not spoken to the UFC about the matchup.
Topuria announced he plans to return to full training in January and hopes to fight again between April and June of 2027.
body: Ilia Topuria is interested in doing The Ultimate Fighter (TUF) alongside Paddy Pimblett ahead of his UFC return.

Topuria is set to fight again in the first half of 2027, having almost fully recovered from the broken bones he sustained when he lost the lightweight title to Justin Gaethje at UFC White House in June.
Topuria suffered his first career defeat against Gaethje but is feeling more motivated than ever ahead of his return Getty
Last month, Pimblett suggested that coaching against bitter rival Topuria on the reality TV show produced by the UFC would set the perfect foundation for their mega-fight.
Topuria and Pimblett have long been linked to meet in the UFC ever since the pair got caught up in an altercation at a London hotel in 2022.
Both UFC stars even faced off in the Octagon after Topuria knocked out Charles Oliveira to become the new lightweight champion last year.
With Pimblett coming off a career-best win over Benoit Saint Denis in July, it feels like there is no better time to book what could be one of the UFC’s biggest fights ever against Topuria.
Although Topuria has made it clear he wants a rematch with Gaethje, he recognises his timeline for a UFC return would work perfectly to take on Pimblett in TUF.
Topuria talks Pimblett on TUF
Speaking to One On One MMA with talkSPORT’s Adam Catterall this week in his first English interview since losing to Gaethje, Topuria said: “I heard something about that [TUF].
“They want to do it, me against Paddy. Nothing official. I haven’t spoken with anyone from the UFC just to clear it up.
“But, yeah, it’s something that could happen. Why not?”
The 29-year-old and talkSPORT’s No. 6 pound-for-pound UFC fighter added: “It would be a huge fight [against Pimblett].
“As I told you, you put me against anyone right now, and I’m going to change their lives financially.
Topuria believes he is the money in the UFC’s lightweight division right now Getty
A fight against Pimblett would be one of the biggest in UFC history Getty
“And the bad part is that I’m going to change their lives physically also.
“Because they are going to face a man that has seen everything in this sport.
“Nothing fears me.”
When is Topuria returning to UFC?
Topuria said he will make a full return to contract training in January.
In the months since his Gaethje defeat, the Georgian-Spanish fighter has only been able to run and do strength and conditioning.
“Once I get back to training in January, let’s see how I’m going to feel, how my body is going to respond,” Topuria concluded.
Topuria believes he will be ready to fight again in April, May or June Getty
“I believe that my body is going to respond to me well, as always, and everything is going to be alright.
“If everything is alright, I’m going to get back in the Octagon in April, May, June, something like that.”
What is The Ultimate Fighter?
TUF is a reality TV show that offers up-and-coming fighters the chance to fight for a UFC contract while being coached by the sport’s biggest stars.
The first season aired in 2005, and its gripping finale between Forrest Griffin and Stephan Bonnar is largely credited with saving the UFC from bankruptcy and putting the company in the mainstream.
The last series, TUF 34, concluded at UFC Vegas 121 in September.
Tina Black, coached by Daniel Cormier , won the women’s strawweight bracket, while Ilimbek Akylbek, coached by Michael Bisping , was crowned the winner at men’s bantamweight.
UFC Schedule

There are still several blockbuster shows and exciting contests for fight fans to look forward to in 2026, and you can find the full list of all confirmed events and official bouts as part of talkSPORT.com’s UFC schedule .
The UFC, on average, puts on 13 to 14 premium events in a calendar year, with up to 30 smaller ‘Fight Night’ cards allowing prospects and less experienced fighters to showcase their talents.
On January 1, 2026, Dana White’s promotion signed a seven-year broadcast deal with CBS and Paramount+ for exclusive rights in the US, meaning the UFC has put on shows like never before this year.

With the historic first event in the new Paramount era, UFC 324, delivering huge success, and a one-of-a-kind fight card at the White House in June opening up the UFC to a new audience, the promotion remains a premium global sports brand, and fans are eager to keep track of results and upcoming fights.

articles.headline: Netflix Officially Removes Clint Eastwood’s R-Rated War Thriller
keyFacts: Netflix removed the Clint Eastwood war thriller American Sniper at the beginning of November in the United States.
The film has moved to a new streaming home on Peacock in the United States.
Peacock subscribers have limited time to watch the movie, as it is scheduled to leave the service on December 1.
body: While Clint Eastwood is often associated with the Dirty Harry franchise and Westerns such as The Good, The Bad and The Ugly, The Outlaw Josey Wales, and Unforgiven, as a director, he's frequently explored stories of war. After directing Heartbreak Ridge in 1986, Eastwood returned to war stories in a big way in the 2000s, with back-to-back World War II movies Flags of Our Fathers and Letters from Iwo Jima.

In 2014, Eastwood made what appears to be his final war film — he is 96 years old, after all — the Bradley Cooper-led biographical war drama-thriller American Sniper. After an extended stint streaming on Netflix, Eastwood's blockbuster war thriller has moved to a new streaming home.

In the U.S., Netflix removed American Sniper at the beginning of November. The war thriller has since found a new streaming home on Peacock in the U.S., and is available to stream on Netflix and HBO Max in other territories.

American Sniper stars Bradley Cooper as U.S. Navy SEAL Chris Kyle, and is based on the autobiographical book about "the most lethal sniper in U.S. military history." Cooper earned one of his 12 Academy Award nominations for American Sniper, which was also up for a Best Picture Oscar at the 2015 ceremony.
What is American Sniper about?

The adaptation of Kyle's memoir isn't just about the Iraq War or the Navy SEAL's prowess with a rifle, it's about the toll that multiple deployments take on a soldier and the people around him. Here's American Sniper's official synopsis:

U.S. Navy SEAL sniper Chris Kyle is sent to Iraq with only one mission: to protect his brothers-in-arms. His pinpoint accuracy saves countless lives on the battlefield and, as stories of his courageous exploits spread, he earns the nickname "Legend." However, his reputation is also growing behind enemy lines, putting a price on his head and making him a prime target of insurgents. Despite the danger, as well as the toll on his family at home, Chris serves through four harrowing tours of duty in Iraq, becoming emblematic of the SEAL creed to "leave no man behind."

American Sniper also stars Sienna Miller as Taya Kyle, Luke Grimes as Marc Lee, and Jake McDorman as Ryan Job. The movie also infamously stars a plastic baby as one of the Kyles' children in a scene that was heavily mocked at the time. According to American Sniper screenwriter Jason Hall, Eastwood was forced to use the immersion-breaking doll after two infants planned for the shoot had to bow out.

Fake plastic baby notwithstanding, critics and Academy members loved American Sniper. On Rotten Tomatoes, the film has a 71% Tomatometer score based on 302 critic reviews. American Sniper was nominated for six Academy Awards, including Best Actor (for Cooper), Best Adapted Screenplay, Best Filming Editing, Best Sound Editing, and Best Sound Mixing. The film secured just one Oscar, though, for Best Sound Editing.
Eastwood fans have limited time to watch American Sniper on Peacock, however. The film is set to leave NBCUniversal's streaming service on Dec. 1.

articles.headline: Looking at Xbox, You Can See Everything
keyFacts: Xbox CEO Asha Sharma stated that console sales remain constrained by supply despite readily available hardware in stores and online.
Industry analyst Mat Piscatella stated that he is not seeing results from Xbox's new strategy and that recent decisions have lost engagement.
Sharma stated on CNBC that Xbox aims to reach halfway to its long-term daily-player goal by Financial Year 2030 with sustained double-digit growth.
body: Like many people who have watched Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim’s masterful documentary You Can See Everything, I sat down with my friend after our screening to bounce our thoughts off of one another. The film revolves around convicted felon Elizabeth Holmes, the former CEO of Theranos who was criminally indicted for defrauding investors, and her husband Billy Evans, who met her some time after the charges against Holmes were made, picking up their story a month before her incarceration.

The documentary is about a lot of things, but at its core, the main question it posits is whether Holmes is a master manipulator or is being masterfully manipulated by the men in her life, with multiple parallels drawn between her husband Evans and her former partner, both romantically and in business at Theranos, Ramesh "Sunny" Balwani.

At the end of the conversation I was having with my friend, I came to the conclusion that it was a Schrodinger’s Cat kind of situation; Holmes is both a master manipulator and has found herself in partnerships with other master manipulators, and therefore, she is always manipulating but also always being manipulated, all at once. I then came to a more straightforward answer: You Can See Everything is about two people whose heads are so firmly up their own asses, and each other's asses, that they form an ouroboros, with no way to tell where one of them begins and the other ends.

On the subway ride home from the theater, I was going over the news that I had missed in the day, including Microsoft’s latest financial report, which revealed that, once again, Xbox hardware revenue had declined year-over-year. Following this announcement, Xbox CEO Asha Sharma gave a similar explanation that she has used in the past, saying the reason sales were down was due to a lack of supply of Xbox consoles to meet demand.

In such close proximity to viewing You Can See Everything, a three-hour film that lays bare, quite literally in one scene, what delusion looks like, this comment from Sharma was the latest in a long line of quotes and business decisions that in the moment made me think, "Here is a company with its head very firmly up its ass."
Why would she deceive you?

At the time of this writing, if you live in the United States and go to Microsoft’s own online store , you can buy any iteration of either the Xbox Series X or S, new or preowned, and have it shipped in the next few days. Anecdotally, many of my colleagues and I have seen plenty of consoles, from each of the big three hardware manufacturers, in retail stores local to us. Many peers in the industry who live outside the US, such as former GameSpot editor Kevin VanOrd (Belgium), state that Xbox consoles are readily available for them, both online and in stores. In fact, I cannot find a single instance of anyone online claiming they cannot find an Xbox console.

One of the things that You Can See Everything fixates on, and was central to Holmes's cases, was her telling investors that the device Theranos made was able to test drops of blood for any disease. In Holmes' stated view, the Theranos device could do any blood test with one drop of blood eventually , once the technology for each test had been developed. In reality, when Theranos was courting investors, the device only had access to data for a dozen or so tests at that moment in time, and even then, there were numerous errors in its output.

Sharma’s exact quote around hardware is: “Console sales remain constrained by supply, with more demand than consoles available.” The most reasonable reading of this statement would be that any Xbox console that makes it to a shelf is being sold immediately due to incredible demand from consumers, and that the company cannot keep up the manufacturing pace. But there is so much readily available evidence to that not being true, so how else could this statement possibly be read?

Perhaps supply is not referring to the consoles themselves, but to the supply of components meant to make them. Despite all its money and power, even Microsoft must be having a hard time sourcing hardware to manufacture its consumer products as compute cost continues to climb due to vastly ramped-up data-center construction. Sure, there are Xbox systems on shelves, but it's probably more difficult for Microsoft to stock those shelves than it was a few years ago.

And then there’s the part about there being more demand than consoles available. Technically, you could claim without a clear indicator, such as empty shelves, that the demand is there. Certain retailers have stopped carrying Xbox consoles, like Costco, citing “business decisions.” While there’s no clarity on what those business decisions are, it would be hard to imagine they would stop selling Xbox consoles if they were selling well. So perhaps there are people who do want to buy an Xbox, but nowhere locally stocks the hardware, not due to supply but a conscious choice on the part of the vendor. There could be a big group of people who desire to buy an Xbox but can’t because of affordability, as the consoles are now hundreds of dollars more expensive than they were nearly six years ago, when supply truly could not meet demand. This is, fortunately for Xbox, something you could claim, but it's impossible to prove.

Looking at these words in this light is an absolutely bizarre and unnatural way to read Sharma’s statement, but that doesn’t mean the argument for that interpretation couldn’t be made, much in the same way that Holmes claims she meant something completely different from what investors comprehended. Even in her explanation of the Theranos device to Fielder in the film, it takes tremendous pushback on the part of the documentarian to extract what she really means when she says the hardware "can" run any kind of test. And when he tries to get Holmes to understand how her words could be interpreted dissimilarly, and let’s be honest, more realistically, Holmes’ defense is that she just is different from, and thinks differently than, everyone else. Again, something that is impossible to prove.

In the film, all while Holmes prepares for incarceration, she and Evans are making plans for what Evans dubs Theranos 2.0. The film flits between numerous scenes of them discussing ideas, on phone calls with partners, and waxing poetic about the technology’s potential. This breathless montage feels eerily similar to the exhaustive changes that have occurred at Xbox in 2026. It hasn’t even been nine months since the announcement of Phil Spencer’s departure , and the company has laid off thousands of employees, closed or parted ways with several studios, overhauled its Game Pass subscription multiple times, pivoted Project Helix from a singular console to a “family of devices,” created Mythical Achievements, partnered with Hideo Kojima on his Physint project, walked back the company’s multi-platform ambitions, launched its disc-to-digital program, spun up the vibes-based Xbox Labs seemingly overnight, and of course the most impactful change of all, switching its branding from Xbox to XBOX.

While I will be the first to admit that Xbox needed a radical shake-up after Spencer’s lumbering, methodical, studio-absorbing reign, that revamp needed to be more akin to taking a few crucial, calculated shots with a sniper. While some choices have felt like that, such as the collapsing of the company’s bloated management structure, most of the decisions have felt more like panicked shotgun blasts you take immediately after ducking behind cover. In most games, those kinds of shots don’t get you very far, and according to industry analyst Mat Piscatella, the same is true for Xbox’s new strategy.

“In terms of actual results, I’m not seeing anything right now. And I’m looking really hard,” he said in the latest episode of The Game Business . Even the calculated shots, such as removing Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 from Game Pass to incentivize sales, haven’t panned out in the immediate, with Piscatella claiming the franchise has “lost a ton of engagement” due to that decision.

As Holmes and Evans enter the final days of the former’s freedom, the two discuss the logistics of how they’ll continue to have business meetings while Holmes is incarcerated, with the hope that they’ll have a working prototype of a new blood-testing contraption in under a year. It’s a moment that you watch with your head in your hands in disbelief. Surely no one could be this out of touch? How do they fail to grasp the reality of the situation they are in?

While Xbox, and to an extent the gaming industry at large, is more wounded than it has ever been, Sharma envisions a world where a billion people engage with the Xbox brand every day--a vision that, no matter how much I crunch or fudge the numbers , is nigh impossible to realize. As I write this article, a new Sharma quote hit the timeline from an interview on CNBC . “By Financial Year 2030, our ambition is to be halfway to our long-term daily-player goal with sustained double-digit growth in players and engagement and industry-leading margins,” said Sharma. To be confident in this wildly ambitious goal while the industry is going through an unprecedented, prolonged phase of uncertainty and instability is a crystal-clear example of the meme phrase, “You can just say things.”

Of course, internally, Xbox has access to a ton more data with which to build a clearer picture than those of us on the outside do. And the choice to hide that additional information is intentional. Back in the days of the Xbox 360, Microsoft used to reveal sales numbers for its consoles because they were selling well. That all stopped in the early days of the Xbox One, when it was clear that device was struggling.

Since Sharma became CEO of Xbox, there has been a new kind of transparency, however. For every major change at the company, she and chief content officer Matt Booty have publicly shared the emails they’ve sent to employees informing them of the next stage of Xbox’s reset. While there have been some hard facts revealed in those emails, like the brand’s recent margins only hovering at around 3%, the company only reveals so much to give the appearance of being transparent.

Tangentially, the company is leaning much harder into engaging with followers on social media and making decisions seemingly based on their whims, such as the XBOX rebrand. There’s a huge difference between this behavior versus genuinely listening to your fanbase and internalizing feedback. The latter informs your decision-making, but shouldn’t define it. The former is nothing more than pandering to an audience: one that the company is all too aware will fight on the brand’s behalf on the social-media frontlines.

This window Xbox is offering into its new reset is almost like the company inviting you into its space and saying, well, you can see everything. However, despite gaining that level of access, there’s always the potential of masterful manipulation, because the truth is, you cannot see everything. You are not allowed to see everything, because if you did, things would be much clearer as to exactly what state the company is in. You can see everything, including the fact that you cannot. Therefore, it becomes impossible to discern fact from fiction, and ultimately, you’re left with the feeling that the company can’t even discern that difference for itself.

articles.headline: Trump fires Susie Wiles after midterm blowout, names Stephen Miller as new chief of staff
keyFacts: President Trump announced on Truth Social that Susie Wiles is leaving her role as Chief of Staff to move to the Trump Political Operation.
Trump named Deputy Chief of Staff Stephen Miller as the new Chief of Staff, effective Monday, November 9, 2026.
White House officials indicated that the leadership change reflects a combative approach to upcoming Democratic congressional investigations following midterm losses.
body: “I am pleased to announce that Mr. Stephen Miller, the current Deputy Chief of Staff of the Trump Administration, and one of my most trusted advisors, will become the Chief of Staff starting Monday, November 9, 2026,” Trump wrote on Truth Social.
“Susie Wiles, who has done an outstanding job, will be moving over to the Trump Political Operation. I want to thank her for her service as Chief of Staff — She has done a great job!”

Wiles, 69, managed Trump’s successful 2024 campaign and was credited with bringing stability and cohesion to the West Wing during her 21-month tenure, during which she was diagnosed with breast cancer.

Miller, 41, has served as deputy chief of staff for policy, acting as a key conduit with federal agencies. His wide portfolio ranged from pushing forward Trump’s mass deportation campaign to overseeing the release of declassified UFO files.
Trump’s selection of Miller reflects his likely combative approach toward defending his policies and fighting Democratic congressional investigations next year.
“There are still many who are gearing up for the challenge. It’s time to fight even harder,” a White House official told The Post ahead of Trump’s announcement.

“Serving President Trump in the White House has been the honor of a lifetime,” Wiles said on Friday. “I’m so proud to have been a part of what we’ve accomplished together from securing our border and cutting taxes to strengthening our economy and putting America First.

“More than anything, I’m grateful for the extraordinary people I’ve had the privilege of working alongside. While my role may be changing, my commitment to the President and the mission never will,” she added.

Other potential heads to roll after the midterm loss include Secretary of War Pete Hegseth and Adm. Brad Cooper, commander of US Central Command, for their roles overseeing the Iran war, which fueled the landslide changeover in legislative power.
